title: Hangsúly és intonáció
summary: Stress is always on the first syllable. Yes/no questions rise on the second-to-last syllable and then drop.

sections.text: Every Hungarian word is stressed on its **first syllable**, however long it is: **va**gyok, **é**lek, **be**szélek, **ta**nulok, **kí**vánok, **ö**rülök.
Long vowels (á, é, ó…) are **not** the same as stress. In be**szé**lek the é is long, but the stress is still on **be**.
In a sentence, the **important word** carries the main stress, and the verb after it is said lightly: **Ma**gyar vagyok. · **Ma**gyarul beszélek. · **Lisz**szabonban élek. · **Ta**nár vagyok.
A question without a question word is said with the same words as a statement. Only the melody changes: the voice **rises on the second-to-last syllable** and drops on the last one.

items.en: Does he live in Budapest? (rise on -ten, drop on él)
Are you an engineer? (rise on va-, drop on -gy)
Do you speak Hungarian? (rise on -ya-, drop on -rul)

sections.text: If the question has only one or two syllables, the rise and fall squeeze into the last syllable: *Igen?* *Tényleg?*
